summary: [spec fidelity] ATIP ruling: an output that declares no fields makes --fields USAGE. A batch export with --fields is not refused up front. `canon export --input '[{"kind":"subject","output":"b1.json"},{"kind":"subject","fields":"recordCount"}]'` passes the plan pass (it reads the item against ExportPreviewReport, whose paths hold recordCount) and fails at element 1 in the run pass (read against ExportReport): BATCH_INCOMPLETE with element 0's file already written (seen). "fields":"id" (or argv --fields id with an --input array) is refused in the plan pass with expected [dryRun,kind,output,recordCount], the preview's paths, so no fields value can succeed in a batch. BatchExportReport declares no fields, so --fields on a batch should be USAGE field --fields (or /items/N/fields) before any write. Blast radius: only export has a batch output; no test binds the batch path (atip.paging.13 never reads --input). The brief puts --input-supplied --fields in 0.35; the up-front refusal and no partial write are due now.
